parts: Sulekha, the fourth daughter of Numberdar Ramlal, is called Bholi, 'the simpleton'. A fall from her cot at ten months damaged her brain; smallpox at two left her body covered with pock-marks. She could not speak till five and then stammered, so children mocked her and she spoke little. Her parents worried that no one would marry her.

When a primary school for girls opens, the Tehsildar tells Ramlal, as a revenue official, to set an example by sending his daughters. Ramlal's wife says that educated girls cannot be married off, but agrees to send Bholi: there is little chance of her marrying anyway. Bholi is bathed and given a cast-off dress; frightened, she thinks she is being sent away like the cow that was sold.

At school the teacher speaks to her softly, pats her and gives her a picture book. She promises that in a month Bholi will read it, and that if she studies she will lose her stammer and be respected by all. Bholi feels hope for the first time.

Years pass; the village grows into a small town. A rich but lame, middle-aged grocer, Bishamber, with grown-up children, agrees to marry Bholi without dowry. At the wedding he lifts her veil, sees the pock-marks and demands five thousand rupees. To save the family's honour Ramlal pays, putting his turban at Bishamber's feet.

Bholi throws the garland away and refuses to marry so mean and greedy a man. She speaks clearly, without stammering. She tells her father to take back his money and says she will look after her parents in their old age and teach in the school where she studied. The teacher watches with deep satisfaction.
Themes: girls' education, the effect of love and encouragement on a neglected child, dowry and greed, self-respect and empowerment.
K. A. (Khwaja Ahmad) Abbas wrote in English, Hindi and Urdu, wrote the screenplay of Mera Naam Joker and won the National Film Award four times. His autobiography is I Am Not an Island (1977).

Present perfect (have/has + past participle) links the past with the present; simple past for finished actions; past perfect (had + past participle) for the earlier of two past actions. Noun ↔ verb forms (consultation — consult, humiliation — humiliate).
